rule.title: Strict Enforcement of Layer Isolation (No Layer Skipping)
rule.statement: Requests must flow strictly through defined architectural layers: Route -> Controller -> Service -> Repository/Prisma. Upper layers must not bypass intermediate layers.
rule.rationale: Bypassing layers prevents centralized security filtering, audit logging, transaction demarcation, and data normalization.
rule.implementation_guidance: Express controllers must only call Service methods. Never invoke prisma queries directly in controllers.

forbidden.example: export async function getDoc(req, res) { const doc = await prisma.document.findUnique(...); res.json(doc); }

preferred.example: export async function getDoc(req, res) { const doc = await docService.get(req.params.id); res.json(doc); }

source.evidence_quote: Layers of isolation means that changes made in one layer of the architecture generally do not ripple through to other layers... closed layers enforce this boundary.

rule.title: Avoid Architecture Sinkhole Anti-Pattern
rule.statement: Do not construct redundant pass-through layers that perform no calculation, validation, transformation, or orchestration.
rule.rationale: When 80% of service methods do nothing but call repository methods with identical parameters, layered abstraction adds pure boilerplate without value.
rule.implementation_guidance: For simple read-only data fetches, allow Controller to invoke an Open Query Gateway directly rather than building empty 5-line wrapper services.

forbidden.example: Controller -> DocumentService.get() -> DocumentManager.get() -> DocumentRepo.get() with identical arguments and no logic.

preferred.example: A dedicated DocumentQueryService returning formatted DTOs directly.

source.evidence_quote: The architecture sinkhole anti-pattern occurs when requests flow through multiple layers of the architecture as simple pass-through processing with little or no logic performed within each layer.
